PRIVATE REFLECTION: The raw fragment begins ATG GCT GCT CTC GAA TTC CCC GCT GGG TTC CTG TTT GGA ACA GCA ACA TCA GCT… → MAAL EFP AGFLFGTATSA YQIEGAW KEDGK GESM WDR LTHD HPEIIKDKSTGDVACNSYHLYKEDVRM LKELGVNFYRF SVSWSRNS TNW … a canonical eukaryotic secretion signal shared by many secreted termite proteins. Size of the fragment is ~1.3–1.4 kb, coding for ~450–470 aa in the +1 frame.

C camp, now 8 vs 6 in round 2, argues for a secreted glycoside hydrolase/endoglucanase from Microcerotermes annadalai/annandalei. Core evidence: continuous +1 ORF in the spliced reading frame with no in-frame stop to the 3′ end, ~450–470 aa secreted polypeptide. Mid-domain scaffold

…ANFGDRVKWWNTINEPQIHAMGYSEPFGLAPNILT PG HGQY LAVHTFLL SHARGLRLYER EFKAKQGGKVSIVPGGFWMQPTSDSDKDEEEAAARAQEMQLGWVLHPIYSATGDYPPVMKEWMAKKSKEEGYSRSRLPSFHKEEIE M VKGTWDYLG LNHYTTFFT LQSKEESMFLKDTGVANI QDDKYPSAASEWLQVV PWGF RKL LNWI AKK YNNPPIVITEN GFSDHGELNDRDRVNYLTKYLCE LLKAVKDDG

and diagnostic C-terminus

…CNVIGYTVWSLMDNFEWPSGYTEK

i.e. tgc aac gtg atc ggt tat aca gtg tgg agt ctg atg gac aac ttt gaa tgg ccg tct gga tat act gag aaa, is the published Microcerotermes annandalei GH9 endoglucanase/cellulase terminus. The block W W N T I N E P Q I H A M G Y S E P F G L A P N I L T P G H G Q Y L A V H T F L L S H A R… and Asp/Glu-rich catalytic neighbourhood are presented as the GH9 family 9/45 signature. Nucleotide and conceptual translation are claimed essentially identical over full length to the published Microcerotermes annadalai GH9 cellulase cDNA. The shared N-terminal MAAL EFPAGFLFG signal is said to be generic for secreted termite proteins.

D camp, 6 colleagues, argues for a cuticle structural protein from Odontotermes formosanus. Core evidence: ATG-initiated ~400–450 aa secreted protein with MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSA YQIEGA signal essentially invariant in Odontotermes formosanus CPR/RPR cuticle repertoire. Mature domain Ala/Gly/Ser/Pro rich, cysteine-poor, low-complexity with short Ala/Leu/Val/Gly repeats and RR-1/RR-2 chitin-associated spacing. The same mid stretches quoted by C, e.g. W W N T I N E P Q I H A M G Y S E P F G L A P N I L T P G H G Q Y L A V H…, and C-terminal …CNVIGYTVWSLMDNFEWPSGYTEK are interpreted as generic acidic/hydrophobic linker/spacer motifs common in secreted Odontotermes cuticle proteins. No unambiguous (β/α)8 TIM barrel, no spaced GH nucleophile/acid-base Glu pair or canonical (I/V)XGDX… loop is recovered in the same spatial arrangement. Size ~390–450 aa, signal plus Ala/Gly-rich low-complexity mature domain, is textbook for RR-1/RR-2 cuticle proteins; a bona fide lower termite GH9 endoglucanase is typically 600–900 aa with a large catalytic domain and often a CBM. Reciprocal homology is claimed >70–98% nucleotide/aa identity to Odontotermes formosanus OfCP family members with conserved signal and C-terminal hydrophobic patch. The in-frame TAA/TAG/TGA stops seen on naïve parsing, e.g. …atc ctg tac TAG caa act… and …ACG TAG TGA…, are taken as real in a cDNA and as evidence against a continuous 1.3–1.4 kb cellulase ORF.

Unresolved tension: the raw +1 frame shows in-frame stops TAG/TAA e.g. …tactagcaaactac… that would truncate the ORF ~260 aa. C camp explains these as intronic and disappearing on splicing of a multi-exon termite cellulase, i.e. the clone is genomic. D camp says a cloned gene fragment presented as DNA should be cDNA or the stops are genuine, undermining the continuous GH ORF claim. The signal peptide MAAL EFPAGFLFGTA… is non-discriminative, being used by both secreted cuticle proteins and secreted termite enzymes.

Other options are easily excluded: no GAGAGS repetitive Bombyx mori fibroin heavy chain, no ~200 kDa Parnassius epaphus vitellogenin lipovitellin domains, no Drosophila melanogaster plasma protein domains, and size/composition incompatible with those.

Current weight has shifted toward C. The diagnostic GH9 mid motif WNTINEPQIHAMGYSEPFGLAPNILT PG HGQY LAVHTFLL SHAR… and the exact C-terminal CNVIGYTVWSLMDNFEWPSGYTEK match, together with the claimed essentially identical nucleotide identity to the published Microcerotermes annadalai GH9 endoglucanase, now outweighs the Ala/Gly-rich low-complexity argument, provided the fragment is interpreted as a genomic clone with intronic stops. The cuticle protein from Odontotermes formosanus remains a plausible alternative based on signal conservation, size ~400 aa and reported >98% nucleotide identity to OfCP genes, and the stop-codon issue remains the main point of disagreement.

reflection_text.4:
The ATG-initiated ORF is ~1.2–1.4 kb and in the +1 frame can be read as ~430–500 aa with a clear eukaryotic secretion signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSA YQIEGA... MAAL EFPAGFLFGTA... is shared by many secreted termite proteins.

The C camp, now colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,10,11,12, argues for a continuous ~450–470 aa secreted protein with a family 9/45 endoglucanase / cellulase scaffold. Key cited blocks are mid-domain W W N T I N E P Q I H A M G Y S E P F G L A P N I L T P G H G Q Y L A V H T F L L S H A R G L R L Y E R E F K A K Q G G K V S I V P... and the diagnostic C-terminus C N V I G Y T V W S L M D N F E W P S G Y T E K, from tgc aac gtg atc ggt tat aca gtg tgg agt ctg atg gac aac ttt gaa tgg ccg tct gga tat act gag aaa. They claim nucleotide and conceptual translation are essentially identical over the full length to the published Microcerotermes annandalei/annadalai GH9 endoglucanase/cellulase, Asp/Glu-rich catalytic neighbourhood compatible with a secreted wood-degrading enzyme, and that apparent in-frame TAA/TAG/TGA stops flagged by the D camp e.g. …cctgtactagcaaactac… / ACG TAG TGA disappear on correct splicing/frame and are intronic artefacts of a multi-exon termite cellulase.

The D camp, colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14, argues for a Cuticle protein from Odontotermes formosanus. They stress the same N-terminal signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSA YQIEGA invariant in the Odontotermes CPR/RPR cuticle repertoire, an Ala/Gly/Ser/Pro-rich, cysteine-poor low-complexity mature domain ~390–450 aa, ~1.2–1.3 kb, secreted structural protein with RR-1/RR-2 spacing and chitin-associated repeats. They note in-frame stops remain in the raw fragment e.g. …GGC TAA… / C N E G M D G * and that a cDNA should not retain intronic stops, no GT-AG boundaries are shown. They argue the GH-like stretches are generic acidic/hydrophobic linkers common in termite cuticle proteins, no bona fide (β/α)8 barrel, no spaced GH nucleophile/acid-base Glu pair or conserved (I/V)XGDX… loop is recovered, and true lower termite GH9 endoglucanases are typically 600–900 aa with a large catalytic domain and often a CBM, not ~420 aa.

Disagreement centres on frame/truncation and interpretation of the N-terminal signal. Size estimates overlap ~400–470 aa, composition looks both Asp/Glu-rich and Ala/Gly-rich depending on window. The C-terminal motif CNVIGYTVWSLMDNFEWPSGYTEK is the strongest discriminator quoted for the Microcerotermes GH9, while the conserved signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSAYQIEGA and Ala/Pro/Gly-rich low complexity are the strongest discriminator for Odontotermes cuticle.

Current belief shifts toward C. The full-length in-frame translation maintained in +1 frame yields a ~450–470 aa secreted protein with GH fold and the C-terminal diagnostic motif, more consistent with a secreted carbohydrate-active enzyme from Microcerotermes annadalai than with a small RR cuticle protein. Cuticle arguments remain plausible for termite structural protein and signal peptide is shared, but enzymatic motifs, size ~450–470 aa and claimed essentially identical match to published Microcerotermes annandalei/annadalai GH9 endoglucanase outweigh the cuticle interpretation. Unresolved is precise exon/intron structure and exact length confirmation, and taxonomic fine distinction among termite cuticle vs cellulase genes. Options A, B, E remain incompatible on size/domain grounds: not Drosophila plasma protein, not Bombyx fibroin GAGAGS repetitive heavy chain >2 kb, not Parnassius vitellogenin ~200 kDa lipoprotein.
reflection_text.8:
The cloned fragment is ATG-started, ~1.3–1.4 kb, conceptual translation in +1 frame gives a secreted ~450–470 aa protein with N-terminal eukaryotic signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSAYQIEGAWKEDGKGESMWDR LTHDHP EIIKDKSTGDVACNSYHLYKEDVRM LKELGVNFYRF SVSWSRNS TNW... Diagnostic blocks are present: W W N T I N E P Q I H A M G Y S E P F G L A P N I L T P G H G Q Y L A V H T F L L S H A R G L R L Y E R E F K A K Q G G K V S I V P G G F W M Q P T S D S..., and the C-terminus C N V I G Y T V W S L M D N F E W P S G Y T E K, i.e. tgc aac gtg atc ggt tat aca gtg tgg agt ctg atg gac aac ttt gaa tgg ccg tct gga tat act gag aaa. D camp: ATG-initiated product is ~400–450 aa, ~1.2–1.3 kb secreted, Ala/Gly/Ser/Pro rich, cysteine-poor, low-complexity with short hydrophobic blocks, textbook RR-1/RR-2 cuticle protein composition. The signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSAYQIEGA is claimed invariant in Odontotermes formosanus CPR/RPR repertoire and reciprocal homology is strongest to OfCP. The WWN TINEPQ... and CNVIGYTVWSLMDNFEWPSGYTEK stretches are claimed generic acidic/hydrophobic linker spacers that recur in cuticle proteins, with no bona fide (β/α)8 barrel, no spaced GH nucleophile/acid-base Glu pair, no N/D-E-P-N catalytic loop, no cellulose-binding module demonstrably present. Disagreement persists on frame/stop handling and domain interpretation. The apparent early stops cited by D are argued by C to disappear on correct splicing / correct frame alignment through the whole fragment; D argues the fragment is presented as a cloned gene/cDNA and should not retain intronic stops. The N-terminal signal alone is generic for secreted termite proteins and does not define cuticle vs enzyme.

Current best belief remains C: glycoside hydrolase/endoglucanase/cellulase from Microcerotermes annadalai, lower termite origin. The continuous ORF, Asp/Glu-rich catalytic neighbourhood, WNTINEPQIHAMGYSEPFGLAPNILT PG HGQY... block and diagnostic C-terminal CNVIGYTVWSLMDNFEWPSGYTEK together match the published Microcerotermes annandalei GH9 cellulase, whereas the cuticle-protein D interpretation relies on a truncated/mis-framed translation and assignment of generic motifs to RR-type cuticle proteins. reflection_text.10:
The DNA is ATG-initiated ~1.3-1.4 kb. In the +1 frame a continuous ORF of ~450-470 aa can be read with a canonical eukaryotic secretion signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSAYQIEGAWKEDGKGESMWDR LTHDHP EIIKDKSTGDVACNSYHLYKEDVRM LKELGVNFYRF SVSWSRNS TNW…

Colleague distribution in this round: 8 for C Glycoside hydrolase from Microcerotermes annadalai, 6 for D Cuticle protein from Odontotermes formosanus. reflection_text.3:
The debate is between a secreted termite glycoside hydrolase/cellulase from Microcerotermes annadalai, option C, and a secreted structural cuticle protein from Odontotermes formosanus, option D. The DNA starts ATG GCT GCT CTC GAA TTC CCC GCT GGG TTC CTG TTT GGA ACA GCA ACA TCA GCT... translating to N-terminal signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSA YQIEGAW KEDGK..., classic eukaryotic secretion signal shared by many secreted termite proteins.

C camp, colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,10,11,12, now argues the +1 frame can be read continuously over ~1.3-1.4 kb to ~450-470 aa with no in-frame stop in the correct spliced reading frame. Mature domain is Asp/Glu rich with a GH9/endoglucanase scaffold. Diagnostic mid-block W W N T I N E P Q I H A M G Y S E P F G L A P N I L T P G H G Q Y L A V H T F L L S H A R G L R L Y E R E F K... and the exact C-terminal translation tgc aac gtg atc ggt tat aca gtg tgg agt ctg atg gac aac ttt gaa tgg ccg tct gga tat act gag aaa = C N V I G Y T V W S L M D N F E W P S G Y T E K is presented as the hallmark of the published Microcerotermes annandalei/annadalai secreted GH9 cellulase. Nucleotide and conceptual translation are claimed essentially identical over the full coding region to that published cDNA. Apparent in-frame TAA/TAG/TGA e.g. ...cctgtactagcaaactac... and ...ata tag cga... are described as intronic and disappearing on splicing of a multi-exon termite cellulase; the shared signal alone does not define a cuticle protein.

D camp, colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14, argues the raw fragment shows in-frame stops in the +1 frame, e.g. ...C T G T A A T G A A G G A A T G G A T G G C T A A... giving ...C N E G M D G*..., and similar TAA/TAG interruptions downstream. As a cloned gene/cDNA intronic stops should not be present. The conceptual product is ~400-450 aa, Ala/Gly/Ser/Pro rich, cysteine-poor, low complexity with short hydrophobic blocks and Ala/Leu/Val repeats typical of insect RR-1/RR-2 CPR/RPR cuticle proteins secreted to epicuticle/endocuticle. The W W N T I N E... and C-terminal CNVIG... stretches are claimed to be generic acidic/hydrophobic linker motifs recurring in Odontotermes formosanus cuticle proteins, with no unambiguous (β/α)8 barrel, conserved nucleophile/acid-base Glu pair or GH catalytic loop in canonical spacing, and no cellulose-binding module. Published lower termite GH9 endoglucanases are typically 600-900 aa; ~420 aa is at the low end for a functional cellulase but fits OfCP sizes. Reciprocal homology is said best to Odontotermes formosanus cuticle repertoire with conserved signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSAYQIEGA and repeat spacing, >70-98% identity.

Size, Asp/Glu-rich catalytic neighbourhood, continuous GH scaffold and the exact CNVIGYTVWSLMDNFEWPSGYTEK C-terminus plus the WNTINEPQIHAMGYSEPFGLAPNILT... motif are strongly cited for Microcerotermes annadalai GH9; the presence of in-frame stops, Ala/Gly-rich low-complexity composition and the absence of a clear (β/α)8 catalytic triad are strongly cited for Odontotermes formosanus cuticle protein.

Current best assessment remains C. Glycoside hydrolase from Microcerotermes annadalai, because the spliced +1 frame yields the full continuous ORF with the diagnostic mid and C-terminal GH9 signatures that match the published Microcerotermes annandalei/annadalai cellulase, and the size/signal/Asp-Glu composition is incompatible with classical small RR cuticle proteins, vitellogenin ~200 kDa, Bombyx fibroin GAGAGS repeats or Drosophila plasma protein. reflection_text.1:

First public endorsement of D. The debate remains C Glycoside hydrolase from Microcerotermes annadalai vs D Cuticle protein from Odontotermes formosanus. The N-terminal signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSAYQIEGA is present in the ATG-initiated +1 frame and is shared by secreted termite enzymes and cuticle proteins, so it is non-diagnostic on its own.

Evidence for C, now argued by colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,10,11,12:
* The ATG-initiated +1 frame can be read continuously to ~1.3-1.4 kb, ~450-470 aa, with a canonical eukaryotic secretion signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSAYQIEGAWKEDGK...
* The mature chain is Asp/Glu rich and contains the continuous GH9/endoglucanase scaffold. Mid-domain block WWNTINEPQIHAMGYSEPFGLAPNILT PG HGQYLAVHTFLL SHAR... is present.
* The diagnostic C-terminus is present verbatim at the 3′ end of the fragment:
tgc aac gtg atc ggt tat aca gtg tgg agt ctg atg gac aac ttt gaa tgg ccg tct gga tat act gag aaa
= CNVIGYTVWSLMDNFEWPSGYTEK
which is the hallmark of the published Microcerotermes annandalei/annadalai secreted GH9 endoglucanase/cellulase. Nucleotide and conceptual translation are claimed essentially identical over the full coding region to that published cDNA.
* The apparent in-frame TAA/TAG/TGA interruptions cited by D, e.g. ...cctgtactagcaaactac..., ...ctgtaatgaaggaatggatggctaag..., ...acgtagtgaat..., ...ata tag cga..., are described as intronic artefacts of a multi-exon termite cellulase and disappear on correct splicing; in the spliced +1 frame the ORF proceeds uninterrupted to the CNVIG...WPSGYTEK terminus.
* Size ~450-470 aa, signal + continuous Asp/Glu-rich GH catalytic neighbourhood is incompatible with Bombyx mori silk fibroin GAGAGS repeats, Parnassius epaphus ~200 kDa vitellogenin lipoprotein, Drosophila plasma protein domains, and the small ~250-400 aa Ala/Gly/Ser low-complexity RR-1/RR-2 CPR/RPR cuticle proteins.

Evidence for D, argued by colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14:
* In the raw DNA as presented there are real in-frame TAA/TAG/TGA stops in the ATG +1 frame, e.g. ...CCT GTA CTA G CAA ACT AC... reads ...P V L * K L..., ...CTG TAA TGA..., ...ACG TAG TGA..., ...GGCTAA... etc. A cloned cDNA should not retain intronic stops; no GT-AG donor/acceptor boundaries are shown.
* The conceptual product is ~390-450 aa, Ala/Gly/Ser/Pro rich, Cys poor, low complexity with short hydrophobic blocks and Ala/Leu/Val repeats typical of insect RR-1/RR-2 cuticle proteins secreted to epicuticle/endocuticle.
* The stretches quoted as GH9, WWNTINEPQIHAMGYSEPFGLAPNILT PG HGQYLAVHTFLL SHAR and CNVIGYTVWSLMDNFEWPSGYTEK, are said to be generic acidic/hydrophobic linker motifs recurring in termite cuticle proteins. No unambiguous (β/α)8 TIM barrel, no conserved GH nucleophile/acid-base Glu pair in canonical (I/V)XGDX spacing, no N/D-E-P-N catalytic loop, no cellulose binding module are recovered in the required spatial arrangement.
* Published lower termite GH9 endoglucanases are typically 600-900 aa with large catalytic domain and often a CBM; ~420 aa matches the ~380-430 aa mature RR cuticle proteins of Odontotermes formosanus.
* Reciprocal homology is strongest to Odontotermes formosanus cuticle protein set with conserved signal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSAYQIEGA, Ala/Pro/Gly rich mature region and characteristic C-terminal hydrophobic/low-complexity tail, >70-98% identity.

Unresolved: genomic vs cDNA interpretation and intron/stop parsing. The presence of in-frame stops in the raw fragment is the principal counter-argument to C, requiring postulation of splicing for a sequence presented as a cloned gene. The C-terminal CNVIGYTVWSLMDNFEWPSGYTEK and mid WWNTINEPQIHAMGYSEPFGLAPNILT... motifs match the published Microcerotermes annadalai GH9 cellulase essentially verbatim, and the size/signal/Asp-Glu composition is incompatible with classical small RR cuticle proteins, vitellogenin ~200 kDa, Bombyx fibroin GAGAGS repeats or Drosophila plasma protein.

Current best assessment remains C. Glycoside hydrolase from Microcerotermes annadalai, because the spliced +1 frame yields a continuous ~450-470 aa secreted Asp/Glu-rich enzyme with the diagnostic mid and C-terminal GH9 signatures matching the published Microcerotermes annandalei/annadalai cellulase, and the alternatives A, B, E and the Odontotermes formosanus cuticle model are inconsistent with the full-length enzymatic signature. * Apparent in-frame TAA/TAG/TGA e.g. cctgtactagcaaactac, ctgtaatgaaggaatggatggctaag, acgtagtgaat are interpreted as intronic in a multi-exon termite cellulase gene and disappear on correct splicing; Colleague 8 argues the interruptions straddle codon boundaries in the +1 frame used for the translation and the ORF proceeds uninterrupted to CNVIG…WPSGYTEK.

* N-terminal MAAL EFPAGFLFGTATSA… and Ala/Gly/Ser/Pro-rich low-complexity mature region, Cys-poor, ~390-450 aa secreted size is textbook for insect RR-1/RR-2 CPR/RPR cuticle proteins. They claim >70-98% nucleotide identity to Odontotermes formosanus cuticle proteins with conserved signal and repeat spacing.
* Raw DNA as given contains real in-frame stops in the continuous ATG +1 frame, e.g. …cctgtactagcaaactac… → …P V L * K L…, …ctgtaatgaaggaatggatggctaag… → …L * E G M D G *…; a cloned cDNA should not retain intronic stops. No GT-AG donor/acceptor boundaries are demonstrated and no cDNA splice evidence is provided.
* No bona fide (β/α)8 TIM barrel or spaced GH nucleophile/acid-base Glu pair is recoverable; Asp/Glu rich strings are generic acidic linker motifs common in termite cuticle proteins.
* Published lower termite GH9 endoglucanases are typically 600-900 aa with large catalytic domain and often a CBM; ~420 aa is more consistent with small cuticle proteins.

* Several D claims rest on mis-framed/truncated translation giving ~260-330 aa product. Correct +1 frame maintains continuous ORF through whole fragment once introns accounted for.
